newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian firms see Q1 profits down - ABS.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian firms see Q1 profits down - ABS.

text.p: Australian businesses expect profits to fall 2.9 percent in the March quarter from the previous quarter, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said on Thursday.
This compared to an expected rise in profits of 3.7 percent in the December quarter 1996 and a fall of 9.6 percent in the previous corresponding quarter last year.
"This is the smallest decrease recorded by this survey for a March quarter," the bureau said in a statement.
The bureau found Australian businesses expected sales to rise 0.4 percent in the March quarter -- the first time the survey has recorded a rise in expectations for the first quarter.
It found capital expenditure was expected to increase 5.8 percent, the biggest expected lift in 12 months.
In the same quarter last year, businesses expected capital expenditure to rise 4.9 percent.
Selling prices were seen 0.1 percent higher, while employment was expected to fall 0.4 percent.
"This is the largest fall in employment expectations since March 1994," the bureau said.
The bureau's survey differs from other business expectations series in that it calculates the volume of expected movements as well as direction.
It does this by asking respondents for the size of expected movements and then weighting the results for the respondent's size.
Each survey, conducted in the middle month of each quarter, asks for expectations for the following quarter.
